artists.biography:
On 24 October 1995, Spacehog released its first album, Resident Alien. It went gold on the Billboard charts, selling over 500,000 copies and spawned the hit single and video "In the Meantime" as well as the single "Cruel To Be Kind". "In the Meantime" received heavy video and radio play, and was used as background music to BBC's Match of the Day football programme. The band performed the song on Channel 4's TFI Friday in 1996. The band's second album, The Chinese Album, was released on 10 March 1998. Though it did not sell as well as Resident Alien, the band's popularity continued to increase as Spacehog opened for more popular acts like Pearl Jam and Supergrass. The Chinese Album had a more "artsy" sound, with the Pink Floyd-like piano on the opening track and Michael Stipe of R.E.M. contributing vocals to the song "Almond Kisses".

After the band was dropped by Elektra Records, Spacehog signed with the upstart label Artemis Records and released its third album, The Hogyssey, on 10 April 2001. The album continued the band's neo-glam approach and included the singles "I Want to Live" and "At Least I Got Laid", as well as a funk version of Richard Strauss's "Also sprach Zarathustra".

perplexity.description:
Resident Alien is the debut studio album by the English rock band Spacehog, released on 24 October 1995 by Sire Records and Hi Fi Recordings. The album is rooted in alternative rock, blending elements of glam rock, Britpop, and classic rock influences with a modern 1990s edge. Its sound is characterized by Royston Langdon’s distinctive vocals, melodic basslines, and the band’s use of synthesizers and organ, creating a rich, textured sonic palette. The album’s most famous track, “In the Meantime,” became a major hit, topping the US Mainstream Rock Tracks chart for four weeks and helping to define the band’s early identity.

As Spacehog’s first full-length release, Resident Alien established the band as a significant presence in the mid-1990s rock scene. The album was recorded live in a barn in Woodstock, New York, lending it an energetic, immediate feel that set it apart from more polished studio productions of the era. It was certified gold in July 1996, reflecting its strong commercial success. Critics praised its catchy songwriting and dynamic performances, and the album remains a cult favorite among fans of 1990s alternative rock.
